answersReviewFindings.finding: Blocking 1: a drain that stops early is never run again while the holder stays live, so copies answered 202 kept expire unread. Only a claim or a keep starts a drain, a keep happens only when no holder is live, and a live holder does not claim again, so every early exit stranded copies: the forward budget, a failed forward that released its claim, a drain that stepped aside for another drain's claim, a failed bus read or cursor write, the drain window, a shutdown.
answersReviewFindings.fix: A drain is now a handover rather than one walk. drainKeptRole loops walkKeptRole, the bounded walk, which reports why it ended; when a walk ends with the lane not drained the handover re-resolves the role's CURRENT holder and walks again: at once for a spent forward or scan budget and for a holder that moved, after roleKeepDrainRetryPause (1 s) for a failed read, a failed cursor write, a failed forward or a released claim, and after roleKeepClaimWindow when it stepped aside for another drain's claim. It stops on a drained lane, on no live holder, after roleKeepDrainIdleRounds (3) walks that forwarded nothing, or at roleKeepHandoverWindow (10 min), which bounds the goroutine; each walk keeps its own roleKeepDrainWindow context, so nothing spins and a role with no holder still costs one resolution.
answersReviewFindings.test: TestOneClaimHandsOverAKeptLaneLongerThanOneWalkOfIt (25 fresh copies, one claim, every copy reaches the one live holder) and TestAKeptCopyWhoseForwardFailedReachesTheHolderWithNoSecondClaim. Both drive the drain through POST /v1/roles/set as production does, rather than calling drainKeptRole, which is what hid the defect; both fail at db64c79daa38.

answersReviewFindings.finding: Blocking 2: the drain forwards to the session it was started for and never checks that this session still holds the role. Concurrent hard claims each start a drain and the one that wins the cursor may be a claimant a later write superseded; and a drain that stepped aside leaves the old drain spending its budget on a session that no longer holds the role.
answersReviewFindings.fix: roleKeepDrainHolds reads cfg.registry.CachedRoleHolder(role) before each copy, so before each claim and before each forward, and ends the walk roleKeepHolderMoved when the claim names another session; the handover then walks again for the new holder. Only a claim naming a DIFFERENT session stops the walk: an unclaimed role and a read that failed are no evidence this walk's session lost the role, since a keep's handover runs for a holder resolved live a moment ago and a release writes no claim.
answersReviewFindings.test: TestADrainStopsWhenTheRoleChangesHolderUnderIt: the role changes holder mid-drain and the copies after the change go to the new holder and not the old one. Fails at db64c79daa38.

answersReviewFindings.finding: Blocking 3 (the architect's decision on the census gap): the Dispatch outbox's role route publishes raw onto the role lane, and the lane now keeps those events where it used to raise no_holder. Dispatch has its own outbox and receipt logic, so a kept copy would be handed to the next holder beside the one Dispatch redelivers.
answersReviewFindings.fix: Dispatch's role publishes are marked keep: false in the envelope the outbox builds, and the lane honours it. The lane reads no keep flag and a raw publish carries none, so the envelope is the only channel: one optional field, keep, on the envelope contract (TypeScript, the JSON schema, regenerated into Go), documented as the flag a sender that keeps its own queue sets on a message it publishes straight onto a role lane. Absent still means keep, so no other publisher changes, and publishRoute sets it on the role branch alone.
answersReviewFindings.test: TestARoleRoutedEventTellsTheRoleLaneToKeepNothing (outbox) and TestTheRoleLaneKeepsNothingForASenderThatKeepsItsOwnQueue (listener: keep:false raises no_holder and stores nothing; no flag is still kept).

answersReviewFindings.finding: Prose: the census missed two senders, and neither the Change list nor any changelog fragment mentioned that concurrent hard claims now all answer 200 where the losers used to get a 500.
answersReviewFindings.fix: The census gains both rows with their disposition: the Dispatch outbox's role route (opted out this round, per the decision above) and packages/envoy-plugin/src/server.ts:146 (unaffected; it returns the client's whole result to the model as JSON and reads no status). answersReviewFindings.fix: One roleKeepLaneCursor type holds the sequence and both writes, so the write-and-check block appears once (3797a4ae). One refusedRoleForwardOutcome switch serves the lane and the drain, and a forwarded kept copy finishes through finishRoleForward, so it counts in envoy_messages_delivered_total and records the dedupe as a lane forward does (3797a4ae). isValidRole moved into keepForNextHolder, the one keep both give-up paths take, so route and lane agree by construction (3797a4ae). forwardAndWait is a method of listenerDeliveryHandlerConfig and forwardKeptRoleMessage is the receipt-timeout check over it (3797a4ae). keepForNextHolder starts the drain itself, so no give-up path can keep a copy without offering it to the current holder (3797a4ae). bus.consumerFilterSubjects drops any subject overlapping the kept prefix and migrateLegacyConsumerFilters uses it, so a migrated legacy notifications.> consumer never gets a kept copy or a cursor body (3797a4ae). trickyParts: The handover must not spin and must not outlive its purpose: it stops on a drained lane, on no live holder, after three walks that forwarded nothing, and at a ten-minute bound, with each walk keeping its own one-minute context.

Only a claim naming a different session ends a walk for a holder that moved. Treating an unclaimed role or a failed read as a loss would end the handover a keep just started, since a keep's drain runs for a holder resolved live a moment ago and a release writes no claim.
The role lane reads no keep flag from a request, so Dispatch's opt-out had to travel in the envelope. Absent means keep, so the flag costs nothing to any other publisher.

A forwarded kept copy now goes through finishRoleForward, which records the attempt before the forward and clears it when the forward failed; without that the drain's retry would read its own attempt as a reason to skip the copy.
deviations: The claim window's clock (review minor) is answered rather than changed. The age compares one listener's clock with the stream's store time, and the assumption that they are within a minute is stated in roleKeepClaimWindow's doc with what it costs and what measuring would buy: a round trip per walk, to guard against a listener so far out of step that it also drops every copy as past roleKeepWindow, where the cost of being wrong is the duplicate the design already accepts. Offered to the reviewer to take the round trip if it prefers.

The phase reminder's kept-answer branch is kept rather than deleted, in the second shape the reviewer offered: EnvoyPublish is typed to Pick<PublishResult, "kept">, so the unknown probe is gone, and the doc says the branch is unreachable today and why it is read all the same. Round 1's test for it stays meaningful.
The base was merged forward again at the architect's instruction, so the merge ref carries sjawhar/legion#2598 and #2594; it needed no conflict resolution.
discoveredComplexity: A drain started by a claim or a keep was the whole of the design, and nothing else ever starts one. That is why every early exit stranded copies: the fix had to be a scheduler, not another exit path.
